T0615.title: Credential Reuse
T0615.definition: The repeated use of the same login credential, session token, or access credential across multiple devices, network environments, or account usage contexts.
T0615.description:
Credential reuse may come from normal multi-device login, but it can also indicate account sharing, cookie resale, bulk login after credential stuffing, or session-token theft. After attackers obtain account passwords, cookies, tokens, or one-time login states, they can reuse those credentials on their own devices to access business systems, bypass normal login flows, or scale account abuse.

In risk-control contexts, credential reuse focuses on whether the relationships among credentials, devices, IPs, User-Agents, geolocation, and behavior chains are abnormal. For example, the same cookie appearing in multiple regions within a short period, frequent device-fingerprint changes for a token, or one account concurrently performing high-value actions on multiple terminals may indicate that credentials are being shared, resold, or stolen.
T0615.usageExample: The platform found the same account cookie being used concurrently on multiple unfamiliar devices, and combined the device-fingerprint changes to determine credential reuse risk.
